How to choose a coffee machine for your kitchen

The best-value machine is the one that makes your usual drink without turning every morning into a project. Start with the number of cups, how you like your coffee and how much preparation and cleaning you are happy to do.

Filter, espresso, bean-to-cup or pods?

A filter machine is worth comparing when you want a jug of black coffee for several people. A manual espresso machine suits someone willing to learn dosing and preparation; check whether a grinder is included or needs buying separately. Bean-to-cup machines reduce some preparation but still need cleaning. Pods can simplify drink preparation, but check the compatible capsules, their ongoing cost and the drinks the exact model makes.

Check the coffee format as carefully as the machine price. De’Longhi’s guidance, for example, distinguishes coarser ground coffee for filter machines from finer espresso grounds and says instant coffee should not be used in its machines. Source: De’Longhi coffee-format guidance. Follow the instructions for your exact model.

A coffee machine for a small kitchen: measure the working space

Measure width, depth and the height beneath cupboards. Then allow room to lift a water tank, open a bean hopper or filter lid and remove the drip tray. A compact footprint is less helpful if the machine must be pulled out every time you refill it. Check your normal mug height and the manufacturer’s installation clearances too.

Milk drinks: think about the second cup

For regular cappuccinos or lattes, check whether the machine has a steam wand, an automatic milk system or requires a separate frother. Consider the steps needed to prepare two drinks and clean the milk parts afterwards. A pump-pressure headline alone does not tell you how convenient the whole routine will be.

Compare the cost per morning, not just the machine

Add the likely cost of beans, ground coffee or capsules, plus any grinder, filters and manufacturer-approved maintenance supplies. Count the drinks you actually make each week. A cheaper appliance can become the more expensive choice if its consumables cost more or you need extra equipment to make your preferred drink.

Cleaning and refurbished buying checks

Check access to removable parts, the descaling instructions and availability of replacement filters, jugs or seals. For refurbished stock, confirm condition, included accessories, warranty and returns; an espresso machine missing its portafilter or milk jug may need additional spending. Product reviews are most useful when they describe the exact model, drink and cleaning routine you plan to use.

eBay UK vs Amazon UK: where should you compare?

For Coffee Machines, it is worth checking both retailers rather than assuming one is always cheaper. eBay UK can be useful for new, refurbished and open-box stock and exposes seller feedback clearly. Amazon UK can be useful for comparing new-stock availability, delivery options and retailer returns where offered. Always compare the exact model number, condition, warranty, delivery cost and returns policy before deciding.

Buying questions answered

Is a filter coffee maker better than an espresso machine?

Choose by the drink and routine you want. Filter coffee suits a jug of black coffee; espresso preparation and milk drinks involve different equipment, ingredients and cleaning.

What should I check for a coffee machine in a small kitchen?

Check cupboard height as well as the footprint, access for refilling and cleaning, cup clearance and the manufacturer’s installation requirements.

Does an espresso machine include a grinder?

Some do and some do not. Check the exact listing and supported coffee format, then include a suitable grinder in the budget if needed.

Are pod machines always cheaper to use?

Compare the cost of compatible capsules with the beans or grounds for your usual number of drinks. Purchase price alone cannot settle it.

What matters when buying a refurbished coffee maker?

Confirm the exact model, condition, included brewing and milk accessories, cleaning requirements, warranty and returns.
